stem: A particle moves along the $x$-axis with $x=2t^3-9t^2+12t$ ($x$ in metres, $t$ in seconds). Select all correct statements.
solution:
$v=6t^2-18t+12=6(t-1)(t-2)$ so $v=0$ at $t=1,2$ (A true) while $v(1.5)=-1.5\ne0$ (D false). $a=12t-18\Rightarrow a(1)=-6$ (B true). $x(3)=54-81+36=9$ and $x(0)=0$ (C true).

stem: A $2\ \mathrm{kg}$ block is pushed up a rough incline of angle $\theta$ with $\sin\theta=0.6$, $\cos\theta=0.8$ and coefficient of kinetic friction $0.5$, by a force parallel to the incline so that it moves up at constant speed. With $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, the force required in newton is
solution:
Constant speed: net force zero along the incline, friction acts down the slope: $F=mg\sin\theta+\mu mg\cos\theta=20(0.6+0.5\times0.8)=20\ \mathrm{N}$.

stem: A small block slides from rest from the top of a smooth fixed hemisphere of radius $90\ \mathrm{cm}$ and leaves the surface at some point. The vertical distance (in cm) of that point below the top is
solution:
At angle $\theta$ from the vertical: energy gives $v^2=2gR(1-\cos\theta)$; radial equation $mg\cos\theta-N=mv^2/R$. It leaves when $N=0$: $\cos\theta=2(1-\cos\theta)\Rightarrow\cos\theta=\tfrac23$. Drop $=R(1-\cos\theta)=R/3=30\ \mathrm{cm}$.

stem: A mixture of $2$ mol of a monatomic ideal gas and $3$ mol of a rigid diatomic ideal gas is kept at moderate temperature. The ratio $C_p/C_v$ of the mixture is

stem: Two satellites circle the same planet. Satellite A has orbital period $3\ \mathrm{h}$. Satellite B moves in a circular orbit whose radius is $4$ times that of A. The period of B in hours is
solution:
Kepler's third law: $T^2\propto r^3\Rightarrow T_B=T_A\,4^{3/2}=3\times8=24\ \mathrm{h}$.

stem: The velocity of a particle moving along a line is $v=t^2-6t+8$ (SI units). The total distance travelled in the interval $t=0$ to $t=5\ \mathrm{s}$ is
solution:
$v=(t-2)(t-4)$ changes sign at $t=2$ and $t=4$, so split the path. With $x(t)=\frac{t^3}{3}-3t^2+8t$: $x(2)=\frac{20}{3},\ x(4)=\frac{16}{3},\ x(5)=\frac{20}{3}$.

Distance $=\frac{20}{3}+\left|\frac{16}{3}-\frac{20}{3}\right|+\left|\frac{20}{3}-\frac{16}{3}\right|=\frac{28}{3}\ \mathrm{m}$. ($\frac{20}{3}$ is the displacement, not the distance.)

*Verified by: recomputed-by-code.*

stem: Masses $3\ \mathrm{kg}$ and $5\ \mathrm{kg}$ hang from the two ends of a light string passing over a smooth light pulley. Taking $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, the tension in the string (in newton) is
solution:
$a=\dfrac{(5-3)g}{8}=2.5\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. For the lighter block $T-3g=3a\Rightarrow T=3(10+2.5)=37.5\ \mathrm{N}$. Check with the heavier block: $5g-T=5a\Rightarrow T=50-12.5=37.5$.

stem: A simple pendulum has period $T$ in a stationary lift. In a lift accelerating upward at $3\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ (take $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$) its period becomes $T'$. The ratio $T'/T$ is approximately
solution:
In the lift's frame $g_{eff}=g+a=13\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. $T\propto g_{eff}^{-1/2}\Rightarrow T'/T=\sqrt{10/13}=0.877$.

stem: A $500\ \mathrm{kg}$ satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius $2R_E$ about the Earth ($R_E=6.4\times10^6\ \mathrm{m}$, $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ at the surface). The minimum extra energy needed to free it from the Earth's gravity is
solution:
Total energy in orbit $=-\dfrac{GMm}{2r}$; to escape it must become $0$, so $\Delta E=\dfrac{GMm}{2r}=\dfrac{gR_E^2m}{4R_E}=\dfrac{gR_Em}{4}=\dfrac{10\times6.4\times10^6\times500}{4}=8\times10^9\ \mathrm{J}$.

stem: A stone is thrown vertically upward with speed $20\ \mathrm{m/s}$ from the top of a $25\ \mathrm{m}$ tower and finally lands on the ground at the foot of the tower. Taking $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, the total time of flight in seconds is
solution:
Take upward positive and origin at the throw point: $-25=20t-5t^2\Rightarrow t^2-4t-5=0\Rightarrow (t-5)(t+1)=0$. Only $t=5\ \mathrm{s}$ is physical.
